title: Windsurf Rules (.windsurf/rules) & Cline (.clinerules) Builder
description: Free interactive builder and templates for Windsurf (.windsurf/rules & .windsurfrules) and Cline (.clinerules) coding agent instructions + AGENTS.md sync.
h1: Windsurf rules (.windsurf/rules) and Cline (.clinerules): setup, migration, and live builder.
dek: Generate properly formatted Windsurf Cascade rules, Cline Plan/Act rules, or unified AGENTS.md files in one click—and keep them synced across IDEs.
lede: Windsurf’s Cascade agent and Cline’s Plan/Act extension both let you codify repo standards and agent communication habits in versioned Markdown files—moving beyond single legacy files (.windsurfrules) into modular directories (.windsurf/rules/ and .clinerules/). Below is a live rules file generator plus exact cross-tool compatibility notes.
answer: For Windsurf, store modular Markdown files in .windsurf/rules/ (replacing single-file .windsurfrules) and personal style in Windsurf Global Rules. For Cline, place workspace rules in .clinerules/ (or .cline/rules/)—Cline also auto-reads legacy .windsurfrules and .cursorrules files. To keep multi-agent repos from drifting, anchor shared build/test rules in AGENTS.md.

sections.h2: Production Windsurf & Cline templates (stack + Plan/Act discipline).
sections.html:
1. Windsurf (.windsurf/rules/coding-standards.md)

# Windsurf Cascade Rules <tech_stack> - TypeScript strict mode, React, Tailwind CSS </tech_stack> <communication_and_verification> - Lead with root cause, touched file paths, and minimal diff—keep explanations concise. - Run the test suite after your final edit and report exact command output. - Never introduce new npm dependencies or refactor unrelated files without asking first. </communication_and_verification>

2. Cline (.clinerules/workflow.md)

# Cline Plan & Act Workflow Rules - Plan Mode first: list the exact files you intend to change and the verification command before switching to Act Mode. - Verification gate: run `npm test` (or the repo's targeted test file) after edits and paste exact pass/fail lines. - Communication: state blocking bugs and assumptions first; skip polite filler and generic recaps. - Git hygiene: write concise conventional commit messages when asked to commit.

Migrating legacy .windsurfrules into .clinerules/

mkdir -p .clinerules
cp .windsurfrules .clinerules/windsurf-rules.md

faq.q: Should I use .windsurfrules or .windsurf/rules/ in Windsurf?
faq.a: Use .windsurf/rules/*.md for new projects so you can split tech-stack standards, testing gates, and communication style into small, maintainable Markdown files instead of one monolithic .windsurfrules file.
Yes. Cline natively detects and loads .windsurfrules and .cursorrules in a repository root alongside its own .clinerules/ directory, making cross-tool migration straightforward.

faq.q: Where should I put personal tone preferences so I don't push them to my team's repo?
faq.a: Put personal verbosity, tone, and explanation style in Windsurf Global Rules or Cline's Global Rules / Custom Instructions settings, and reserve committed .windsurf/rules/ and .clinerules/ files for shared repo standards.

faq.q: How do I keep Windsurf, Cline, Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex synced in one repo?
faq.a: Keep your canonical build, test, and architecture rules in a root AGENTS.md file (under ~200 lines) and let tool-specific rule folders focus only on tool-specific behavior like Cline's Plan/Act gate or Cursor's glob rules.
